Getting Started with rlichess

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

rlichess is a modern, tidy R client designed for chess players and data scientists to interact with the Lichess API and analyze chess data using standard tidyverse principles.

Package Architecture

rlichess is structured into three clean layers:

  1. Layer 1: API Clients (lic_*): Direct, transparent HTTP wrappers corresponding 1-to-1 with official Lichess API endpoints.
  2. Layer 2: Tidy Wranglers (lic_tidy_*): Pure offline transformation functions that clean, unnest, and standardize chess data into tidy tibbles.
  3. Layer 3: Chess Analytics (lic_stats_*): Offline statistics and analysis tools (e.g., opening win rates).
[ Lichess REST API ]
        │
        ▼ (Layer 1: API Clients)
  lic_games_user() / lic_user() / lic_explorer_lichess()
        │
        ▼ (Layer 2: Tidy Wranglers)
  lic_tidy_games() / lic_tidy_moves()
        │
        ▼ (Layer 3: Analytics / Visualization)
  lic_stats_openings() / dplyr / ggplot2

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("h8gi/rlichess")

# or using devtools
devtools::install_github("h8gi/rlichess")
library(rlichess)
library(dplyr)

1. Authentication (Optional but Recommended)

While public endpoints can be accessed anonymously, providing a Personal Access Token increases rate limits (up to 30–60 games/sec) and enables on-demand rating history retrieval.

Set your token in your .Renviron file:

LICHESS_API_TOKEN="your_personal_access_token"

In R code, rlichess automatically loads it via lic_token():

lic_token()

2. Layer 1: API Clients

Fetching User Games

lic_games_user() downloads game records directly from the Lichess API in NDJSON format:

# Download recent bullet games since 2025
raw_games <- lic_games_user(
  username = "h8gi",
  perf_type = "bullet",
  since = "2025-01-01",
  max = 50,
  clocks = TRUE,
  evals = TRUE
)

Fetching User Profiles & Rating History 

# User profile summary as a 1-row tidy tibble
user <- lic_user("h8gi")
user %>% select(username, created_at, play_time_total_hours, count_all)

# Performance ratings across game types
perfs <- lic_user_perfs("h8gi")
perfs

# Daily rating history
history <- lic_user_rating_history("h8gi", perf_type = "bullet")

Querying Opening Explorer Databases 

# Query Lichess opening database (e.g. 1. e4 c5)
exp <- lic_explorer_lichess(play = "e4,c5")
exp$moves

# Query FIDE Masters database (2200+ FIDE)
masters <- lic_explorer_masters(play = "e4,c5")
masters$moves

# Query a specific player's repertoire
player_exp <- lic_explorer_player("h8gi", color = "white", play = "e4")
player_exp$moves

3. Layer 2: Tidy Wranglers

Standardizing Game Data

lic_tidy_games() parses raw API output into a user-centric format with POSIXct timestamps, user perspective (user_color, user_result, win), opponent information, and rating differences:

games <- lic_tidy_games(raw_games, username = "h8gi")

games %>%
  select(id, created_at, user_color, user_result, user_rating, opponent_name, opening.name) %>%
  head()

Expanding Move Sequences (Long Format)

For move-by-move analysis (evaluations, clock times, blunders), lic_tidy_moves() unnests games into a long format where each row is a single half-move (ply):

moves_df <- lic_tidy_moves(games)

moves_df %>%
  filter(game_id == first(game_id)) %>%
  select(ply, move_number, color, san, clock, eval) %>%
  head(10)

4. Layer 3: Chess Analytics

Opening Win Rates

Calculate win rates and sample sizes for each opening variation:

stats <- lic_stats_openings(games, min_games = 5)
stats

5. Built-in Dataset

Access the included database of 3,378 ECO openings:

data(lichess_openings)
head(lichess_openings)
